deck_name: 40 - Bare-Metal ARM Assembly, Linker Scripts & Startup

cards.prompt: On an ARM Cortex-M microcontroller immediately after hardware reset, what two 32-bit words are fetched from addresses 0x00000000 and 0x00000004?
cards.answer: Initial Main Stack Pointer (MSP) at 0x00000000 and Reset_Handler vector address at 0x00000004
cards.explanation: Cortex-M hardware automatically loads MSP from word 0 of the vector table and branches to the Reset_Handler address in word 1 (with bit 0 = 1 for Thumb state).

cards.prompt: Why must bit 0 (the LSB) of every function pointer and interrupt vector address in ARM Cortex-M be set to 1?
cards.answer: Cortex-M only executes Thumb/Thumb-2 instructions; LSB = 0 triggers a HardFault/UsageFault (INVSTATE)
cards.explanation: ARMv7-M/ARMv8-M cores do not support legacy 32-bit ARM mode; jumping to an even address clears EPSR.T and faults immediately.

cards.prompt: In a bare-metal GNU ld linker script, what is the difference between a section's VMA (Virtual Memory Address) and LMA (Load Memory Address)?
cards.answer: VMA is where the section runs in SRAM; LMA is where its initial values are stored in non-volatile Flash
accepted_answers: VMA is SRAM runtime address; LMA is Flash storage address
cards.explanation: Initialized globals (.data) have an LMA in Flash and a VMA in SRAM (specified via '> RAM AT> FLASH'), requiring startup code to copy them before main().

cards.prompt: What two memory initialization loops must Reset_Handler execute in C or assembly before calling main()?
cards.answer: Copy .data from Flash (LMA) to SRAM (VMA), and zero-fill .bss in SRAM
cards.explanation: C guarantees that initialized globals hold their initial values (.data) and uninitialized static/global variables start at zero (.bss) when main() begins.

cards.prompt: Why must you wrap the interrupt vector table declaration in __attribute__((section(".isr_vector"), used)) and KEEP(*(.isr_vector)) in the linker script?
cards.answer: To prevent the compiler and --gc-sections linker garbage collector from stripping it as unreferenced data
accepted_answers: prevent linker garbage collection from removing it
cards.explanation: Nothing in C code directly calls the vector table array, so without 'used' and 'KEEP', dead-code elimination deletes the entire vector table.

cards.prompt: In the ARM Architecture Procedure Call Standard (AAPCS), which registers pass the first four 32-bit arguments to a function and hold the return value?
cards.answer: R0-R3 pass arguments; R0 (and R1 for 64-bit) holds the return value
cards.explanation: R0-R3 and R12 are caller-saved scratch registers, while R4-R11 are callee-saved registers.

cards.prompt: Which 8 registers does Cortex-M hardware automatically push onto the active stack upon entering an interrupt service routine (ISR)?
cards.answer: R0, R1, R2, R3, R12, LR, PC, and xPSR
cards.explanation: Because hardware stacks all AAPCS caller-saved registers automatically, standard C functions can be used directly as Cortex-M ISRs without special compiler attributes.

cards.prompt: What is the difference between the ARM Cortex-M instructions 'WFI' and 'SEV'?
cards.answer: WFI (Wait For Interrupt) puts the core into low-power sleep until an interrupt occurs; SEV (Send Event) wakes cores waiting on WFE
accepted_answers: WFI sleeps until interrupt; SEV signals an event
cards.explanation: WFI is standard in bare-metal idle loops to slash current draw while waiting for timer or peripheral interrupts.

cards.prompt: When an STM32 Cortex-M4 triggers a HardFault, which SCB register holds Configurable Fault Status flags (MMFSR, BFSR, UFSR) for diagnosing unaligned access, bus faults, or divide-by-zero?
cards.explanation: Inspecting SCB->CFSR alongside the stacked PC from the fault frame pinpoints the exact instruction and cause of a HardFault.

cards.prompt: What do the Cortex-M instructions 'CPSID i' and 'CPSIE i' do?
cards.answer: CPSID i disables maskable interrupts (sets PRIMASK); CPSIE i enables maskable interrupts (clears PRIMASK)
cards.explanation: Setting PRIMASK = 1 blocks all configurable-priority interrupts during short bare-metal critical sections (while NMI and HardFault remain active).

cards.prompt: Why should you execute a '__DSB()' (Data Synchronization Barrier) after clearing a peripheral interrupt flag inside an STM32 ISR?
cards.answer: To ensure the peripheral write completes over the bus before exiting the ISR so it does not immediately re-trigger
accepted_answers: ensure bus write completes before ISR exit
cards.explanation: Write buffers on the Cortex-M bus matrix can delay the flag-clear write past the ISR exit instruction, causing a phantom second interrupt.

cards.prompt: Given these linker symbols, how many bytes will the startup loop copy for .data?
cards.explanation: 0x20000100 - 0x20000000 = 0x100 = 256 bytes (64 uint32_t words) copied from Flash LMA 0x08004000 into SRAM.
